title: Coleoptera higher-level backbone vs. published phylogenomics
purpose: End-to-end validation of the seqnet -> RuNIE pipeline. No external tool covers the full chain, so the final trees are scored against clades reported in published beetle phylogenomic studies. Clade membership is defined by family; a clade is testable when the run samples >= 2 tips inside and >= 2 outside it. A clade counts as recovered when the unrooted tree contains the corresponding bipartition.

sources.citation: McKenna, D. D., et al. (2019). The evolution and genomic basis of beetle diversity. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 116(49), 24729-24737.
sources.data: 4,818 genes for 146 species; 89 genes for 521 species

sources.citation: Zhang, S.-Q., Che, L.-H., Li, Y., Pang, H., Slipinski, A., & Zhang, P. (2018). Evolutionary history of Coleoptera revealed by extensive sampling of genes and species. Nature Communications, 9, 205.

loci_rationale: The four markers with the widest GenBank coverage across Coleoptera (the 18S/28S/rrnL/cox1 set used for large-scale beetle trees). They are far less informative than the phylogenomic datasets above, so recovery of deep nodes is expected to be partial.

scored_clades.name: Polyphaga (vs. Adephaga)

support.statement: ML analyses separated Polyphaga from Adephaga + Myxophaga + Archostemata

scored_clades.note: With Archostemata and Myxophaga unsampled, this bipartition is identical to Adephaga monophyly.

support.statement: Phytophaga consists of the two highly supported superfamilies Curculionoidea and Chrysomeloidea
Phytophaga (Chrysomeloidea + Curculionoidea) recovered, nested within Cucujoidea
highly supported superfamily (with Chrysomeloidea forming Phytophaga)
highly supported superfamily (with Curculionoidea forming Phytophaga)
Lymexyloidea closely related to Tenebrionoidea with maximal support
Bostrichiformia strongly supported as the sister group of the hyperdiverse series Cucujiformia (BS = 100%)
Elateriformia strongly recovered as the third branching lineage of Polyphaga
Scarabaeoidea, Hydrophiloidea and Staphylinoidea formed a well-supported clade (BS = 94%)

report_only_clades.name: Hydradephaga (Dytiscidae + Gyrinidae)
report_only_clades.why_not_scored: Reported paraphyletic (Zhang2018: recovered as paraphyletic, Bayesian-only support; McKenna2019: paraphyly of aquatic Adephaga).

report_only_clades.name: Staphyliniformia (Staphylinoidea + Hydrophiloidea)
report_only_clades.why_not_scored: Not recovered by Zhang2018 (Staphylinoidea closer to Scarabaeoidea, BS = 78%).

report_only_clades.name: Scarabaeoidea
report_only_clades.why_not_scored: Monophyly not explicitly tested in the cited texts.
